Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

thermify (development version)

thermify 0.1.0

First release. Functional, documented and tested package for agroclimatic thermal indices: growing degree-days, chilling hours, Utah chill units and Dynamic model chill portions, from hourly, daily or monthly temperatures, for single sites and rasters.

Verified on Ubuntu (R release and oldrel), Windows and macOS. Results based on monthly climatologies are model-based estimates; empirical validation against station data is planned (see vignette("validation")).

Breaking changes

  • degree_days() gains method as its third argument and defaults to "single_sine". The previous behaviour (daily average) is method = "average". Name base explicitly in existing calls.
  • chill_hours() gains method as its third argument; lower and upper must now be named when passed by position.

New features

  • Growing degree-days by the average, single/double sine and single/double triangle methods, with horizontal, vertical and intermediate upper cutoffs (degree_days()), and degree-hours (degree_hours()).
  • Chilling hours from daily extremes (analytical sine and triangle, numerical reference) and counted on hourly data (chill_hours_hourly()).
  • Utah model chill units (chill_units(), utah_weights()).
  • Dynamic model chill portions with state carried across blocks (chill_portions()).
  • Hourly reconstruction with the Linvill and continuous sine models (hourly_temperatures(), daylength()).
  • Monthly-to-daily densification through tempify or a native pchip_mp engine, with consistency checks and diagnostics (densify_monthly(), densify_diagnostics(), tempify_available(), tempify_version()).
  • Accumulation periods that may cross the year end (season_days()).
  • threshold_date() returns the date on which an accumulated index reaches a requirement (for example a degree-day or chill-portion target).
  • Progress reporting (blocks, percentage, elapsed time, ETA) in thermify_rast() and for archive downloads, controlled by progress or the option thermify.progress.
  • Integrated workflows for one site (thermify()) and for monthly SpatRaster stacks processed in blocks (thermify_rast()), with GeoTIFF, NetCDF and provenance output.
  • WorldClim 2.1 helpers: worldclim_region() reads 30 arc-second normals for a region (extent or polygon, optional mask) through HTTP range requests on the remote tiles, without downloading global or country files; worldclim_monthly(), study_window(), check_monthly_climate().
  • Cauquenes case study in examples/cauquenes.

Verification

  • Cross-checks against chillR and degday in inst/verification/verify_references.R.

Documentation

  • User stories with acceptance tests (docs/USER_STORIES.md, tests/testthat/test-story-*.R) and a testing strategy (docs/TESTING.md): unit, acceptance, integration and error-path tests, 397 expectations and 94 % line coverage with all optional groups.
